In response to that disaster, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah ordered a province-wide fire safety audit and approved the resumption of annual safety inspections for commercial facilities. An audit conducted earlier this year by the Sindh Building Control Authority revealed that 90% of surveyed buildings in the city's eastern, central, and southern districts lacked adequate fire safety measures, leading to formal notices and the sealing of non-compliant commercial properties in areas like Saddar.

Authorities have not yet officially established the precise cause of the recent fire or calculated the full extent of the financial damage. The market's recurring vulnerability to fires has reignited local concerns about commercial building standards, regulatory enforcement, and emergency response capabilities in densely populated urban zones across Karachi. Investigations and cooling procedures by fire brigade officials remain ongoing at the site of the incident.

stories.title: Power Division and Industry Demand Levy Cuts to Lower Electricity Tariffs
stories.summary:
Representatives from Pakistan's manufacturing sector and the power division jointly called for the removal or reduction of petroleum levies on furnace oil and diesel during a public hearing on Thursday. The discussion centered on a request by the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) for an additional monthly fuel cost adjustment (FCA) of Rs2.56 per unit to recover approximately Rs33 billion for electricity consumed in September. Held by the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra), the hearing addressed industrial concerns that heavy government fuel levies are significantly inflating overall generation costs.

Industrial representatives, including Amir Shaikh, Arif Bilwani, Tanveer Bari, and Rehan Javed, pointed out that the government imposes high petroleum levies of about Rs76,000 per tonne on furnace oil and Rs80 per litre on diesel. They argued that removing these taxes could decrease power generation costs from approximately Rs62 per unit down to a range of Rs44 to Rs50 per unit. Officials from entities under the power division acknowledged the heavy impact of these levies on generation expenses, noting that furnace oil and diesel accounted for 3.6 percent of total power generation in September due to a shortage of liquefied natural gas (LNG) and other cheaper alternatives.

CPPA's Rehan Akhtar reported that actual fuel costs in September reached Rs10.022 per unit compared to the reference rate of Rs7.46, creating the financial shortfall of roughly Rs32.76 billion. However, he maintained that the net increase on consumer bills in November would be limited to Rs1.45 per unit because an existing positive adjustment from October is set to expire. Meanwhile, Nepra officials and industrial participants questioned data transparency, pointing out discrepancies in generation reports and past adjustments related to LNG pricing. Industrial groups also demanded an investigation into coal procurement practices at the Port Qasim power plant over allegations of inflated pricing.

Nepra assured participants that only prudent coal costs would be approved and that producers would absorb any excess expenses. Government entities registered a 6.5 percent increase in overall power demand for September, alongside a 6.7 percent rise in industrial consumption, which industry leaders attributed to a shift from captive generators to the national grid. Naveed Qaiser of the Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC) affirmed that reducing electricity tariffs to enhance industrial competitiveness remains a priority for the government, adding that officials continue to advocate for fuel levy reductions at appropriate forums.

stories.title: First Russian Diesel Shipment Departs for US Following Moscow-Washington Agreement
stories.summary:
The first shipment of Russian diesel bound for the United States since the implementation of a bilateral agreement between Moscow and US President Donald Trump has set sail on a tanker heading toward New York, according to shipping data. Trump announced the arrangement earlier in the month as part of an initiative to lower soaring domestic diesel prices ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections. As part of the pact, Trump waived portions of a recent US sanctions law targeting Russia and threatened European nations with a US diesel export ban unless they released larger volumes from their emergency reserves to alleviate market pressures.

The Malta-flagged tanker Agioi Fanendes loaded 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel at the Russian Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22, according to LSEG shipping information, with an expected arrival in the United States on November 7. Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Limited (EASTMED), the vessel's manager, stated that the ship was awaiting final orders while sailing toward the North Atlantic and that the specific discharging port had not yet been formally finalized. This cargo marks the first direct import by the US since former President Joe Biden enforced a ban on Russian oil and petroleum products in 2022.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed on Friday that the initial vessel under the deal had departed, noting that subsequent shipments would continue at a steady pace. President Trump previously announced on October 9 that Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, to the US and global markets, with an additional 500,000 tons scheduled for November and one million tons to follow thereafter. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak stated that shipments would increase as companies finalize necessary contracts, aiming to restore Russian diesel exports to typical monthly levels of 3 to 3.5 million tons by the end of the year.

Following Moscow's decision to lift its self-imposed ban on diesel exports, shipping data from LSEG and Kpler showed Russian cargoes also resuming voyages to traditional markets such as Turkey and Brazil. Since the European Union enacted a complete embargo on Russian oil products in February 2023 due to the conflict in Ukraine, Russia has primarily diverted its diesel exports to Turkey, Brazil, African nations, and Central Asia via rail. Officials from both nations continue to navigate logistical and contractual frameworks to facilitate the ongoing supply schedule under the newly brokered agreement.

stories.title: US Justice Department Bars FBI and ICE Agents From Monitoring Polling Stations
stories.summary:
The United States Department of Justice announced that agents and personnel from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency will not act as election monitors during the midterm elections. This decision was revealed in a federal court filing responding to a lawsuit filed by the NAACP, a civil rights organization that advocated for racial justice and rights for Black Americans. The lawsuit sought to prevent prosecutors and law enforcement officials from serving as monitors, arguing that the plans devised by the Trump administration amounted to voter intimidation.

According to the court filing, the designated poll monitors will strictly observe polling locations, take notes, and remain prohibited from carrying firearms. The Justice Department emphasized that these individuals have received training to avoid interfering with voting and to strictly adhere to state and local regulations, maintaining consistency with previous practices. While FBI and ICE employees are excluded, personnel from other agencies, including the Federal Bureau of Prisons, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), will participate as monitors.

The policy arrives amidst broader political friction and an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight by the Trump administration, which has pressed states for voter-registration data to ensure public confidence. Meanwhile, political campaigning intensified nationwide as Republican President Donald Trump and Democratic former President Barack Obama assumed prominent roles on the campaign trail. With thirty-five Senate seats and all 435 House seats being contested, nonpartisan analysts favored Democratic chances of capturing the House while viewing the Senate race as extremely close.

Background contexts highlight that Trump's public approval rating dropped near record lows due to public dissatisfaction with high living costs and the war in Iran. Despite this, Trump continued a heavy campaign schedule to bolster Republican turnout, while Obama delivered sharp speeches criticizing the administration. Obama appeared in Morrow, Georgia, near Atlanta, to campaign for Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff against Republican challenger Representative Mike Collins, urging voters to reject corruption and uphold national values.

stories.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Houthi Ballistic Missile and Drone Near Riyadh
stories.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported that its air defenses successfully intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile targeting southern Saudi Arabia alongside a drone in the Riyadh region. These military actions occurred amid a significant escalation of hostilities between the coalition and the Yemeni Houthi group. Separate coalition statements confirmed the destruction of the aerial threats, following a series of similar recent incidents involving cross-border attacks.

The announcements followed earlier coalition reports regarding the interception of another drone over the Makkah region and a cruise missile targeting western Saudi Arabia. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree strongly dismissed the coalition's accounts as false on the social media platform X. Saree stated that the group carried out no operations toward Saudi territory on that day, asserting that their military actions target Saudi oil facilities and military bases rather than civilian areas.

Concurrently, Yemen's armed forces announced they are investigating field reports regarding the alleged Houthi use of projectiles containing toxic substances in the southwestern province of Taiz. The Yemeni Defence Ministry stated that these attacks caused suspected cases of poisoning and suffocation among civilians and resistance fighters. The ministry called for an urgent international investigation, urging the United Nations and relevant organizations to address alleged violations, ensure humanitarian assistance reaches civilians, and hold responsible commanders accountable.

Taiz has remained a central flashpoint in Yemen's ongoing civil war, with government forces and Houthi fighters battling for control of the strategic province for over a decade. The Saudi-led coalition has actively supported the internationally recognized Yemeni government since March 2015, following the Houthi seizure of the capital Sanaa in September 2014. Prolonged restrictions on access routes around Taiz have contributed deeply to the region's enduring humanitarian crisis, which continues to worsen as fighting intensifies.

stories.title: سرینگر میراتھن میں بچے کو ساتھ دوڑانے والی کلثوم بانو کی کہانی
stories.summary:
انڈیا کے زیرِ انتظام کشمیر کے شہر سرینگر میں 25 اکتوبر کو منعقد ہونے والی میراتھن میں 34 سالہ کلثوم بانو نے اپنے ایک سالہ بچے کو جسم کے ساتھ باندھ کر حصہ لیا۔ اس دوڑ میں دو ہزار سے زائد افراد نے شرکت کی اور اس کا آغاز وزیرِ اعلیٰ عمر عبداللہ نے کیا۔ کلثوم بانو کا تعلق گجرات کے ضلع سورت سے ہے اور ان کی شادی سنہ 2012 میں وادی گریز کے امتیاز لون سے ہوئی تھی۔ ان کے شوہر سی آر پی ایف میں ہیں اور اروناچل پردیش میں تعینات ہیں۔ کلثوم اپنے تین بچوں کی اکیلے پرورش کر رہی ہیں اور سرینگر میں جزوقتی فٹنس ٹرینر کے طور پر کام کرتی ہیں۔

کلثوم نے اپنے شوہر کو سرپرائز دینے اور یہ پیغام دینے کے لیے کہ بچوں کی پیدائش کے بعد زندگی ختم نہیں ہوتی، اس میراتھن میں شرکت کا فیصلہ کیا۔ انہوں نے ایونٹ سے ایک دن پہلے اپنے دوست عبداللہ اور کوچ سجاد کے کہنے پر رجسٹریشن کروائی تھی۔ دوڑ کے روز ان کی بیٹی کی طبیعت خراب تھی، لیکن ان کے بڑے بیٹے 12 سالہ عبداللہ نے اپنی بہن کا خیال رکھنے کی ہامی بھری جس سے کلثوم کو حوصلہ ملا۔

دورانِ دوڑ کلثوم نے اپنے چھوٹے بیٹے کو بیبی کریئر کی مدد سے باندھ رکھا تھا۔ راستے میں بھوک سے بچے کے رونے پر وہ لال چوک کے قریب رُکیں اور اسے دودھ پلایا۔ انہوں نے تقریباً تین گھنٹوں میں ہاف میراتھن مکمل کی۔ ان کی یہ ویڈیوز اور تصاویر سوشل میڈیا پر وائرل ہوئیں جس پر لوگوں کی طرف سے مختلف آرا سامنے آئیں، اور کچھ ناقدین نے اس عمل کو بچے کے لیے خطرناک قرار دیا۔

کلثوم اور ان کے کوچ سجاد خان نے تنقید کا جواب دیتے ہوئے واضح کیا کہ بچے کو ساتھ رکھنا ان کی مجبوری اور عزم کا حصہ تھا کیونکہ بچوں کی دیکھ بھال کے لیے کوئی اور موجود نہیں تھا۔ کلثوم کا کہنا ہے کہ وہ سب سے پہلے ایک ماں ہیں اور وہ اپنے بچوں کو مضبوط بنانا چاہتی ہیں۔ اس انوکھے تجربے نے انہیں اور ان کے بچوں کو ایک یادگار لیسن فراہم کیا ہے۔

stories.title: PSL 12 Franchises Approve Retention Rules and Salary Caps Framework
stories.summary:
All eight franchises in the Pakistan Super League have unanimously approved the operational framework for the tournament's 12th edition. Agreements regarding player retention rules, auction regulations, squad structures, and salary caps were finalized during a workshop at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium, led by PSL Chief Executive Salman Naseer.

The player retention deadline has been set for January 13, 2027, allowing teams to evaluate domestic talent during the ongoing National T20 competition. The player auction will follow on January 23, giving franchises a ten-day window to complete their squads. Franchises may retain up to seven players, including direct signings, though teams utilizing the maximum retention must release one player from the previous auction's highest price category into the general pool.

For the auction on January 23, each team will operate under a Rs450 million salary cap. This ceiling increases to Rs505 million for franchises that execute a direct signing, retain their previous season's direct signing, or do both, with a mandatory minimum spend of Rs365 million. The direct signing window remains open until November 23, 2026, allowing teams to acquire one marquee player absent from the tenth and eleventh editions.

Salman Naseer praised the constructive engagement and total openness shown by all eight sides during the line-by-line review of the auction rules. He emphasized that aligning the retention deadline with the domestic T20 matches gives local players a direct opportunity to impact team selections. Further announcements regarding the upcoming tournament are expected in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Netanyahu Bloc Leads Israel Election but Falls Short of Majority
stories.summary:
Final results from Israel's general election show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing and far-right coalition securing 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, with his Likud party maintaining the largest faction with 27 seats. The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, finished behind with 48 seats, while Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List emerged as potential kingmakers by winning a combined 19 seats.

The fragmented outcome leaves both sides well short of the 61-seat threshold required to govern, paving the way for difficult coalition talks or potentially another election. The political stalemate follows unproven allegations amplified by Netanyahu's camp that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding from Qatar to influence the vote-buying operations, a controversy dubbed the 'Raamgate' scandal.

Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of orchestrating an incitement campaign driven by fears of growing Arab political influence. Government officials and the Central Elections Commission provided no evidence of widespread issues, and acting director general Dean Livne dismissed suggestions of widespread irregularities as entirely groundless, though the Shin Bet security service launched a probe into suspected local irregularities.

Opposition figures strongly condemned Netanyahu's actions, with Yair Golan accusing the prime minister of attempting to challenge the election results and Eisenkot stating that Likud had launched a coordinated campaign to delegitimize the vote. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, faces ongoing scrutiny over his past policies regarding Qatari funding in Gaza, setting up a tense period of political negotiations.

stories.title: Oil Prices Rise Toward Fourth Monthly Gain Amid Hormuz Tanker Attack
stories.summary:
Oil prices climbed on Friday, heading toward a fourth consecutive monthly gain as traders reacted to an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and braced for potential conflict escalation following the US midterm elections. December Brent crude futures rose $2.27, or 1.98%, to $117.15 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude climbed $1.79, or 1.75%, to $103.79 a barrel.

The attack in the Strait of Hormuz—a vital sea route for Gulf crude and fuel supplies—involved explosive devices attached by a small boat, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations. The incident added to supply risk concerns as Qatari mediators returned to Tehran to revive stalled peace talks between the United States and Iran, though analysts noted a high likelihood of continued supply disruptions.

Additional regional tensions weighed on markets after Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi sites, including the Ras Tanura refinery, the Rabigh refinery, and an Abqaiq production facility. A Saudi-led coalition also intercepted a Houthi cruise missile over the kingdom's western region. In response to the security environment, executives from ExxonMobil and Chevron cancelled travel plans to a major oil conference in the United Arab Emirates.

Saxo Bank noted that heightened volatility from ongoing elections and Middle East conflicts will likely keep crude trading in a higher range of $70 to $90 a barrel even after hostilities cease. For the month, Brent was on track for a 13% increase, while WTI headed for a 15% jump.

stories.title: Singapore Foreign Minister Praises Pakistan's Constructive Role in Gulf Region
stories.summary:
Singapore's Foreign Minister, Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan, commended Pakistan for playing an incredibly valuable and constructive role in the Gulf during a joint press briefing with Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad. Balakrishnan highlighted the importance of secure maritime routes and adherence to international law, noting that both nations share identical stances on freedom of navigation and the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.

During their delegation-level talks, Dar and Balakrishnan focused on expanding bilateral trade, investment, and exploring opportunities in carbon markets, while acknowledging that current economic ties remain below their diplomatic potential. Dar emphasized Pakistan's commitment to diplomacy, dialogue, and UN principles in resolving global challenges, while also raising concerns regarding the West Bank, humanitarian aid for Gaza, a sovereign Palestinian state, and a peaceful resolution to the Jammu and Kashmir dispute.

Earlier in the day, Dr. Balakrishnan met with Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi. Their discussions centered on regional security dynamics, bilateral cooperation, and mutual strategies to maintain peace and stability, with the Singaporean minister praising the professionalism of the Pakistan Armed Forces.

stories.title: Trump Predicts Swift End to Iran Conflict Amid Rising Gulf Tensions
stories.summary:
Ahead of the November 3 midterm congressional elections, US President Donald Trump stated in a Friday interview with Kansas City radio station KCMO that he believes the war with Iran will conclude soon. Speaking on October 31, 2026, Trump provided no specific details on how the conflict would resolve, but emphasized the necessity of securing a guarantee that Iran will never acquire a nuclear weapon. He also reiterated that the United States would not launch any military strikes against Iran prior to the upcoming elections.

Simultaneously, maritime security incidents escalated in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian Revolutionary Guards Navy reported that three oil tankers caught fire and exploded after attempting to use unauthorized routes, with one crude-carrying vessel hitting a mine. Additionally, Iran claimed it destroyed an unmanned US vessel in the eastern strait. In a separate event, Oman's Royal Navy safely evacuated 25 crew members from a Panama-flagged commercial vessel that suffered a fire 1.6 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam. British navy agency United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations also noted a tanker was disabled by limpet mines on Thursday, though its crew remained safe.

Diplomatic efforts to halt the hostilities continued as Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday in a coordinated push with Washington to negotiate a peace deal. This follows a recent communication sent by US Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei to revive stalled talks. Meanwhile, at the United Nations Security Council, Iran’s representative Gholamhossein Darzi blamed the US and Israel for maritime insecurity, condemning the naval blockade as a violation of sovereignty and international law. Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei separately denounced British attempts to use human rights mechanisms to deflect blame from US and Israeli military actions.

stories.title: Alexander Zverev Reaches World No. 1 Ranking After Years of Resilience
stories.summary:
Alexander Zverev is set to rise to the world number one ranking for the first time in his career when the official ATP rankings are updated. The 29-year-old German secured the necessary points on Thursday by defeating Dutchman Tallon Griekspoor to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open. With Jannik Sinner ending his season prematurely due to an injury, Zverev was already guaranteed to finish the year at the top, marking a milestone after more than a decade on the professional tour.

Born in Hamburg to tennis-playing parents from the former Soviet Union, Zverev's career has featured significant challenges alongside major achievements. He lives with diabetes and faced a career-threatening ankle ligament tear during the 2022 French Open semi-final against Rafael Nadal. Furthermore, he navigated domestic violence allegations from two former partners, which included a German court penalty order in 2023 that was ultimately settled in June 2024 without admission of liability, following an ATP investigation that found insufficient evidence for punishment.

Zverev's professional journey includes capturing his first two Grand Slam titles earlier in the year, adding to a resume that features a gold medal at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics where he defeated Novak Djokovic. He previously reached three Grand Slam finals—at the US Open in 2020, the French Open in 2024, and the Australian Open in 2025. Becoming the 30th man to hold the top spot since rankings began in 1973, Zverev expressed immense satisfaction at achieving the pinnacle of men's tennis despite earlier doubts and setbacks.

stories.title: Everton Defeats Newcastle United to Secure League Cup Quarter-Final Berth
stories.summary:
Everton advanced to the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 victory over Newcastle United at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday. David Moyes’s side established a commanding lead through a 34th-minute goal by James Garner, followed shortly by Hayden Hackney's first strike for the club just before halftime. Thierno Barry added a third goal in the 69th minute to cement the win, while Newcastle's Dan Burn scored a late header in the 88th minute that triggered a brief player brawl. The victory ended a three-match winless run for Everton and set up a quarter-final fixture against fourth-tier side Fleetwood during the week of December 14.

Ahead of the match, Everton announced that winger Jack Grealish was unavailable due to a breach of club discipline following reports of an unauthorized absence from training. Despite his absence, the Toffees controlled the contest, denying early threats from Newcastle players Joe Willock and Fabian Schar through saves by goalkeeper Jordan Pickford. Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle made tactical substitutions at halftime, introducing Joelinton, Anthony Elanga, and Yoane Wissa, but the visiting side's efforts proved insufficient to overturn the deficit.

The upcoming fixture gives Newcastle an immediate opportunity for a response when the two clubs meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday. Everton, who have never won the League Cup and lost in the finals of 1977 and 1984, are chasing their first major trophy since winning the FA Cup 31 years ago. The victory was witnessed from the stands by British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a prominent supporter of the club, as Everton moved one step closer to a potential appearance at Wembley.

stories.title: Afghanistan Spinner Rashid Khan Reaches Historic 200 T20I Wickets
stories.summary:
Rashid Khan made cricket history on Thursday by becoming the first men's player to claim 200 wickets in Twenty20 Internationals. The 28-year-old Afghanistan leg-spinner reached the landmark during the second T20 match against Zimbabwe at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the United Arab Emirates. He achieved the milestone in his 120th T20 international appearance by trapping batter Tadiwanashe Marumani lbw for two runs in the ninth over.

Over the course of his international career in the format, Rashid has maintained an impressive bowling average of 13.96 alongside an economy rate of 6.13. His record features two five-wicket hauls, with career-best figures of 3 runs for 5 wickets. With this latest achievement, the former Afghanistan captain sits comfortably at the top of the all-time leading wicket-takers list in men's T20 internationals, holding a 29-wicket lead over England's Adil Rashid in second place.

The milestone adds to Rashid's growing list of international achievements for Afghanistan. Previously, in October of the preceding year, he also made history by becoming the first bowler from his country to reach 200 wickets in One Day Internationals (ODIs) during a match against Bangladesh held in Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: Australia Nears Test Victory as Spinners Dominate South Africa
stories.summary:
Australia moved closer to a series victory over world Test champions South Africa during the third day of the decider at Newlands Stadium in Cape Town on Thursday, October 29, 2026. South Africa finished the day struggling at 140 for four, holding a narrow lead of 40 runs with six wickets remaining. Australian centurion Josh Inglis highlighted the pivotal dismissal of South African captain Temba Bavuma by spinner Nathan Lyon in the penultimate over of the day after Bavuma batted for nearly three hours to score 35 runs.

Inglis praised Australia's control during the final session, noting that South Africa managed only 87 runs across 34 overs while Lyon maintained continuous pressure to finish with one wicket for 31 runs in 14 overs. South African off-spinner Simon Harmer, who claimed four wickets for 104 runs in 37 overs during Australia's second innings, observed that the pitch changed dramatically, creating greater opportunities for spin. Harmer noted that left-arm fast bowler Mitchell Starc contributed significantly to surface wear through his bowling footmarks.

Fast bowlers also made major contributions for Australia, with Starc dismissing Aiden Markram and Marques Ackerman following his six-wicket haul in the first innings, while Josh Hazlewood removed David Bedingham. Australia was eventually bowled out for 429 earlier in the day, bolstered by 102 runs from Inglis, who only learned he was playing after Steve Smith withdrew due to a neck injury on the morning of the match.

This crucial match determines the outcome of the Test series between two leading global teams, with strategic bowling performances and deteriorating pitch conditions dictating the flow of play. Both sides face immense pressure as the contest heads toward its final stages, making every remaining wicket vital for the final result.

stories.title: Pakistan Raises High-Speed Diesel Price While Petrol Stays Unchanged
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government raised the price of high-speed diesel by Re0.85 per litre on Thursday, bringing the retail cost to Rs400.67 per litre, according to a Petroleum Division notification. Meanwhile, the price of petrol remained fixed at Rs377.91 per litre. The updated pricing becomes applicable on Friday, October 30. The administration continues to apply a levy of Rs114 per litre on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel as part of its revenue collection framework.

The adjustment followed a meeting on Tuesday between Jamaat-i-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, where they discussed public relief measures and the fuel levy. Both sides agreed to establish a joint committee to review expanding an existing fuel relief scheme targeted at owners of motorcycles, rickshaws, and vehicles up to 800cc. Rehman warned that his party would organize a protest march to Islamabad in mid-November if the government failed to announce substantial relief measures by then.

To counter economic pressures stemming from regional conflicts, the government reintroduced several austerity measures, requiring commercial markets to close by 9 PM and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by half for a three-month period. Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik previously announced that the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority would manage daily price adjustments in response to volatile international energy markets, which experienced disruptions following the onset of the US-Iran conflict.

Petrol and diesel serve as primary revenue generators for the state, with monthly sales ranging between 700,000 and 800,000 tonnes. Changes in petrol prices directly affect private commuters, rickshaw drivers, and lower-middle-class transport users, while diesel price shifts impact heavy transport sectors, power plants, and large generators across the country.

stories.title: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari Urges Opposition Participation in Electoral Reforms
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari called on Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf lawmakers to rejoin the electoral reforms committee during a National Assembly session on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Speaking in the lower house, Bilawal emphasized that a powerful parliament requires active participation from all political factions, warning that opposition absence only weakens the legislative institution and prevents proper oversight of governance.

Bilawal urged Leader of the Opposition Mahmood Khan Achakzai to use his authority to ensure opposition lawmakers submit their nominations to the National Assembly speaker's office. He stated that the committee provides a necessary platform to investigate electoral rigging allegations and implement reforms ahead of future elections. Additionally, Bilawal requested official parliamentary briefings regarding national security developments, economic challenges, and the potential implications of recent defence agreements signed by Pakistan.

In response, Achakzai stressed the importance of establishing parliament as the supreme source of power and called for political reconciliation, urging rivals to move past historical disputes and collaborate. Following the assembly session, a high-level PPP delegation consisting of Syed Naveed Qamar and Raja Pervez Ashraf met with Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas Jafri alongside PTI senators to deliver Bilawal's message.

Ashraf highlighted to the media that the opposition leader welcomed the proposal, reiterating that the dignity of parliament is closely tied to ensuring transparent elections. The ongoing dialogue underscores efforts by treasury benches to engage opposition groups in formal legislative committees to address key democratic and security concerns.

stories.title: Faran Tahir Reprises Marvel Villain Raza in Series VisionQuest
stories.summary:
Pakistani-American actor Faran Tahir returned to the Marvel Cinematic Universe after an 18-year absence, reprising his role as the militant villain Raza in the sixth episode of the Marvel Studios streaming series 'VisionQuest'. Tahir originally debuted as Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar in the 2008 film 'Iron Man', where his character kidnapped Tony Stark, played by Robert Downey Jr., before being presumed dead following a betrayal by Obadiah Stane, portrayed by Jeff Bridges.

The unexpected return of the character was first announced in January 2025. In 'VisionQuest', created by Terry Matalas, Raza appears with a transformed aesthetic and a shift in profession. Instead of military fatigues and ties to the Ten Rings organization in Afghanistan, Raza now operates as a bounty hunter in Madripoor wearing a sharp suit and utilizing a specialized earpiece designed to counter high-frequency attacks.

During the sixth episode, the resurrected android Vision, played by Paul Bettany, travels to Madripoor to rescue his reincarnated son Thomas Shepherd, also known as Tommy Maximoff, who was captured by the bounty hunter Paladin. Raza and a heavily armed group arrive at the scene to capture Vision, though Raza's involvement is cut short when Paladin knocks him unconscious during the confrontation.

The series 'VisionQuest' follows Vision's journey of self-discovery following the events of 'VisionVision' while exploring artificial intelligence themes through embedded programming personas. Tahir's reappearance introduces a familiar antagonist back into the modern franchise narrative with renewed capabilities and mysterious new affiliations.

stories.title: Italian Consul General Hosts Pasta Diplomacy Event in Karachi
stories.summary:
Italian Consul General Fabrizio Bielli and his wife, Negar, hosted a "Unite Through Pasta" event in Karachi on Wednesday to celebrate Italian Pasta Day. The global observance, established in 1995 and held annually on October 25, marks a culinary tradition recognized by UNESCO as part of humanity's intangible cultural heritage. Addressing guests in Pakistan, Bielli noted that diplomacy often occurs around dinner tables rather than in formal assembly halls, emphasizing that food serves as a universal language carrying histories, values, and identities.

A key highlight of the evening was the use of olive oil extracted from olives grown in Pakistan, which Bielli pointed to as evidence of over a decade of successful agricultural cooperation and technical assistance between Italy and Pakistan. Commenting on the roughly 600 distinct pasta shapes recognized worldwide, the consul general used pasta as a metaphor for the diplomatic community, illustrating that diverse nations can collaborate to build a peaceful world just as varied ingredients create a harmonious dish.

The event highlighted pasta's historical roots and global reach. Originating from wheat consumed in the East thousands of years ago, pasta was introduced to Sicily by oriental traders during the Middle Ages, eventually becoming a pillar of the Mediterranean diet. Today, it appears in both high-end Michelin-starred restaurants and modest home kitchens. While many Pakistani households frequently prepare spaghetti, the thin vermicelli known locally as seviyan is widely used to make sheer khurma for Eidul Fitr, and filled varieties like ravioli and tortellini are also familiar to food enthusiasts in Karachi.

stories.title: Mohsin Naqvi Claims JUI-F Sought Governor's Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary:
During a heated Senate session on Wednesday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi alleged that leaders of the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) had previously approached the government to request the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Directing his remarks at PTI senators in the House, Naqvi challenged them by noting that JUI-F figures had asked the government to rid them of opponents through state intervention. The comments immediately triggered loud protests from JUI-F lawmakers, including Senator Kamran Murtaza, leading to frequent interruptions from the chair to restore order and stop cross-talk.

Naqvi's claims were part of a broader counterattack against JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, following remarks Fazl made a day earlier regarding the interior minister's recent official visit to Iran. Naqvi strongly denied assertions that Pakistani delegates traveled to Iran to negotiate a defence agreement, clarifying instead that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had assigned him specific responsibilities to manage the ongoing regional war crisis. Expressing frustration over personal attacks, Naqvi stated that Fazl's recent comments had crossed political boundaries and left little room for mutual respect.

The confrontation escalated as Naqvi launched a scathing verbal assault on JUI-F, accusing the party and its leadership of exploiting Islam for political and business gains whenever it suited their personal interests. He further alleged that JUI-F members treat the state as a mother only when they receive government benefits and government shares, but turn against it when left out of power. The interior minister warned that such rhetoric would face a strong response, emphasizing that a clear line had been crossed repeatedly by the party's members.

stories.title: Ben Duckett's 167 Powers England to Consolation Win Over Sri Lanka
stories.summary:
Ben Duckett scored an impressive 167 runs and Liam Dawson claimed four wickets as England defeated Sri Lanka by 55 runs in a One-day International tri-series match at the Gaddafi Stadium on Thursday. Having lost their first three matches of the tournament—including a narrow defeat against Pakistan and a high-scoring loss to Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi—England concluded their campaign with a consolation victory. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka had already secured their spot to face host Pakistan in Saturday's final at the same venue.

Batting first, England posted a formidable total of 386-5 in their allotted 50 overs. Duckett anchored the innings with a 132-ball knock that included 24 fours, while sharing a 163-run opening partnership with Tom Banton, who contributed 74 runs off 75 balls. Additional contributions came from Harry Brook with 44, Will Jacks with 30, Jordan Cox with 43, and an unbeaten 21 from Sam Curran. Sri Lanka's bowling attack suffered under the onslaught, with Eshan Malinga conceding 101 runs in his 10 overs, while Asitha Fernando managed two wickets.

In response, Sri Lanka put up a strong chase but were eventually bowled out for 331 in 45.1 overs. Pavan Rathnayake led the charge for the Islanders with a brilliant 118 off 77 balls, marking his third ODI century of the year against England, supported by Kusal Mendis who scored 89 runs off 71 deliveries. Despite useful middle-order partnerships, Liam Dawson dismantled the chase by finishing with bowling figures of 4-49 from 10 overs, ultimately halting Sri Lanka's momentum and sealing the win for England.

stories.title: Pakistan Coach Hesson Hopes Top Order Excels in Tri-Series Final
stories.summary:
Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has expressed confidence that his side's experienced top-order batters will deliver a strong performance in the upcoming One-day International tri-series final against Sri Lanka at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. Pakistan reached the title clash after claiming three consecutive victories, despite inconsistent contributions from their opening batters, followed by an eight-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka where they were bowled out for 110.

Speaking in a video interview released by PCB Digital, Hesson acknowledged that the team had secured wins even while key players struggled, noting that the squad had yet to play its best game. The batting statistics highlight the early-run struggles, with Fakhar Zaman managing only 31 runs across four innings, former captain Babar Azam scoring 118 runs in the same span, and Saim Ayub contributing 21 runs before being released to return to domestic cricket. In response to these difficulties, opening batsman Maaz Sadaqat was previously called up, and Sahibzada Farhan was brought in as a replacement.

While the top order has faltered, Pakistan's middle order and bowling attack have consistently stepped up. Salman Ali Agha scored a notable 107 against Sri Lanka, Hasan Nawaz contributed 79 against England, and Arafat Minhas added 59. Additionally, an unbroken 113-run innings and a decisive last-wicket partnership by Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf secured a dramatic one-wicket win over England.

Hesson praised the performances of Salman, Hasan, and captain Shaheen Shah Afridi, whose bowling has regularly provided early breakthroughs. Having won 12 out of 19 ODIs since taking charge as white-ball head coach, Hesson remains hopeful that senior players like Babar and Fakhar will use the high-stakes final as the ideal stage to make a decisive, match-winning impact.

stories.title: Pakistan Secures $600 Million World Bank Loan Linked to Reforms
stories.summary:
Pakistan has agreed to a $600 million loan from the World Bank under the Bold Reforms for Investment-Driven Growth and Employment Programme. The overall cost of the initiative is valued at $1.2 billion, with the remaining $593 million funded by the federal government, and the Ministry of Finance overseeing the transaction, which has an estimated approval date of January 29, 2027.

In exchange for the funding, Islamabad has committed to enacting specific laws, including the Investment Act and a new Factoring Law. Additional measures involve establishing a database for outbound workers, permitting free international trade in sugar and wheat, and expanding private sector involvement in urea imports. The World Bank noted that the program aims to address historically low private investment, which stands at around 10 percent of GDP due to regulatory hurdles and trade costs.

The initiative supports broader institutional changes, such as full operationalization of the Pakistan Business Portal, a unified corporate insolvency law, and the activation of the EXIM Bank with a banking license. Furthermore, it targets enhancements for the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan to reach WHO Regulatory Maturity Level 3 and improvements to labor market information systems and vocational training frameworks.

This financial backing arrives as the government pivots toward growth-focused reforms following stabilization achieved via an ongoing International Monetary Fund program. Officials intend to lift private investment to 15 percent of GDP by 2035, helping generate employment for the more than three million citizens entering the local labor market every year.

stories.title: Pakistan Considers Fast-Track Approval for Imported Cotton Seeds
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain has ordered an evaluation of a fast-track approval process for imported cotton seed. The proposed system aims to shorten authorization times to 12 to 18 months, bypassing current procedures that stretch to roughly seven years while maintaining strict biosecurity, biosafety, and scientific testing standards.

The decision emerged from a meeting on the Cotton Revival Strategy held in Islamabad. Attendees examined the persistent drop in cotton cultivation, particularly in the Punjab region, where farmers have increasingly turned to alternative crops like sugarcane and maize due to rising expenses, falling yields, and limited profitability.

To tackle challenges including pest infestations, the Cotton Leaf Curl Virus, and climate shifts, authorities are pursuing a three-pronged approach. This strategy involves reinforcing local seed development, easing improved seed imports, and instituting the expedited clearance mechanism. A dedicated committee led by the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council, alongside the National Seed Development and Regulatory Authority and the Pakistan Central Cotton Committee, will assist in acquiring exotic cotton germplasm.

Additionally, the Department of Plant Protection was instructed to accelerate pending Pest Risk Analyses and Controlled Import Permits. Authorities are currently engaging with several countries to source seeds, relying on responses from international partners including China, which has already submitted its technical dossier.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Extends Recovery with KSE-100 Index Rising
stories.summary:
The benchmark KSE-100 index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange maintained its upward trajectory, posting gains for the fourth consecutive session. Driven by robust buying interest in heavyweight banking and fertilizer companies, the index rose by 1,456.68 points, or 0.88 percent, to close near 167,193.44, marking its highest finish since early October.

Trading activity expanded significantly during the session, with overall volumes reaching 816.83 million shares valued at Rs31.54 billion, compared to 578.12 million shares in the previous trading day. Market breadth remained modestly positive as 232 stocks advanced, 232 declined, and 35 remained unchanged out of 499 traded companies. Foreign investors recorded net sales of Rs1.2 billion.

Major institutional contributors to the index rise included Fauji Fertilizer Company and Habib Bank Limited, while National Bank of Pakistan, D.G. Khan Cement, and Pakistan Oilfields Limited acted as principal drags. Cnergyico Pk led trading volumes with 184 million shares traded, closing at Rs14.08 after gaining Rs1.28, followed by Pervez Ahmed Consultancy and K-Electric.

Corporate earnings reports bolstered market sentiment, with Pakistan Petroleum Limited reporting a 25 percent year-on-year increase in 1QFY27 earnings driven by higher oil prices, and Pakistan State Oil posting a 172 percent earnings surge. Analysts noted that while heavy participation drove the bounce, the index has entered weekly resistance levels, leaving the near-term technical outlook balanced.

stories.title: Pakistan Minister Emphasizes Expanded Export Finance Access for SMEs
stories.summary:
Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani has highlighted the importance of implementing measures to help small and medium-scale enterprises boost exports and secure better access to export financing. During a meeting at the Finance Division in Islamabad, he reviewed feedback from exporters regarding recent government support initiatives.

The state minister underscored the government's objective to support exporting small and medium enterprises by widening financial access, opening foreign markets, encouraging new product creation, and cutting the costs of doing business. Representatives from various sectors participated in the discussions, pointing out hurdles such as taxation and regulatory issues, compliance expenses, certification requirements, and emerging demands for green certifications.

Regarding the Export Finance Scheme utilization, Kayani urged participating banks to assign specific focal persons, clearly outline eligibility guidelines, and establish firm timelines for application processing. He also called for evaluating the feasibility of broadening export credit insurance and setting up risk-sharing mechanisms tailored to smaller exporters.

The consultative meeting served as a platform for officials and business owners to explore practical and actionable solutions to enhance the international competitiveness of domestic small and medium enterprises.

stories.title: Pakistani Finance Minister and Saudi Ambassador Discuss Economic Cooperation
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb recently met with Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, the Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan, in Islamabad. The meeting focused on exploring bilateral economic cooperation, trade, investment, and shared priorities between the two nations. Aurangzeb praised Saudi Arabia's consistent support for Pakistan and highlighted the deep bonds of friendship and brotherhood connecting the countries. The Saudi ambassador emphasized that strengthening business-to-business engagement would deepen people-to-people connections and generate mutually beneficial economic opportunities.

During the discussions, Aurangzeb outlined Pakistan's recent progress in achieving macroeconomic stability. He pointed to enhancements in foreign exchange reserves, lower inflation rates, and recent upgrades by international credit rating agencies. Furthermore, he mentioned Pakistan's re-entry into international capital markets through a recent $3 billion Eurobond issuance alongside access to China's capital market. Both officials explored specific investment prospects in sectors such as agriculture, minerals, and mining, stressing the necessity of turning shared priorities into concrete outcomes to bolster commercial ties.

The conversation also touched upon the regional situation and ongoing conflicts, with both sides underscoring the vital need for peace, stability, and continued cooperation to address emerging challenges. Highlighting Pakistan's strategic geographic location as a potential regional trade and transit hub, Aurangzeb reiterated the government's dedication to pursuing structural reforms and maintaining a predictable investment environment for both domestic and foreign investors. Ultimately, the meeting reinforced the commitment of Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to deepening their strategic partnership.

This high-level diplomatic engagement matters because it reinforces bilateral economic ties and encourages foreign investment in key sectors like agriculture and mining. Stronger commercial engagement helps both nations navigate regional challenges while promoting long-term economic stability and growth for Pakistan as it works to solidify its position as a regional trade hub.

stories.title: Renowned Actor Patrick Stewart Passes Away at Age 86
stories.summary:
Sir Patrick Stewart, celebrated globally for his roles in "Star Trek: The Next Generation" and the "X-Men" film series, has died at his home in Los Angeles at the age of 86. A statement posted to his official X account confirmed that he passed away in the loving care of his wife, Sunny, following a brief journey with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. Memorial contributions have been suggested for the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.

Born on July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, Yorkshire, England, Stewart grew up in poverty with a father who suffered from post-traumatic stress syndrome as a World War II veteran and alcoholism. After a schoolteacher introduced him to Shakespeare at age 12, acting became a safe space for him. He began his professional acting career at 18 and achieved early acclaim as a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s. Despite initial hesitation and advice from his friend Ian McKellen to stay in theater, Stewart accepted the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard at age 47, starring in 176 episodes from 1987 to 1994, several films, and the streaming series "Star Trek: Picard."

Later in his career, he achieved further multi-franchise success by portraying the telepathic, wheelchair-using mutant Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" movie franchise beginning in 2000. Over the course of his illustrious career, he received numerous accolades, including a knighthood bestowed by Queen Elizabeth II at Buckingham Palace in 2010 for his profound contributions to drama. He was married three times and is survived by his wife, Sunny Ozell, and his two children.

Stewart's passing marks the end of an era for science fiction and classical theater enthusiasts alike. From overcoming a difficult childhood in England to becoming a towering figure in global entertainment, his contributions to iconic television and film franchises left an indelible mark on popular culture and inspired generations of fans and actors.

stories.title: Pakistani Collaboration 'Alfaaz' Surpasses 50 Million Spotify Streams
stories.summary:
Pakistani singers Hamza Malik and Zain Zohaib have reached a major musical milestone as their collaborative track "Alfaaz" surpassed 50 million streams on Spotify. Malik shared the achievement on his Instagram story, displaying a total of 50,240,450 all-time streams alongside a celebratory message. Released in July, the romantic track's emotive sound has resonated deeply with listeners, driving its popularity and helping the artists expand their audience footprint well beyond Pakistan's borders.

The song's commercial momentum has been further supported by notable chart performances in key regional markets. An update from Zohaib's official music account indicated that "Alfaaz" climbed to the top spot on Spotify's charts in both Pakistan and India, while also securing the 39th position on the platform's global chart. Additionally, the track appeared at number five on Spotify's Top 10 Songs of the Week, sharing space with international acts like Tate McRae, Olivia Rodrigo, Chappell Roan, ADÉLA, and Mariah Deborah, while also earning recognition on Genius's weekly Top 10.

The track's cultural reach extends far beyond traditional streaming platforms, fueled heavily by viral social media covers. A prominent video shared by Norwegian singer and Quick Style dance member William Gamborg featured children from Lahore's SurTaal Music Academy singing a cover of the track alongside him. Garnering 10 million views on Gamborg's Instagram account, the viral moment underscored the song's widespread appeal. To capitalize on this continuous momentum, the singers recently released an acoustic version of the song.

This milestone is important because it demonstrates the growing global reach of Pakistani musicians and highlights how streaming platforms and social media can bridge international markets. The success of "Alfaaz" in India and its viral reception in Europe illustrate the power of cross-border artistic collaboration in modern digital music distribution.

stories.title: Gold Prices Surge in Pakistan Amid US Federal Reserve Policy Uncertainty
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan experienced a notable increase of Rs3,500 per tola on Wednesday, pushing the domestic rate to Rs425,636 per tola according to data released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). This domestic jump reversed a previous decline of Rs3,001 per tola seen the day before. Similarly, the price for 10 grams of gold rose by Rs3,001 to settle at Rs364,914. Silver prices in the country also saw an upward movement, increasing by Rs61 to reach Rs5,854 per tola.

In contrast to the domestic rise, international gold prices experienced a slight dip, with spot gold edging down 0.3% to $4,044.54 per ounce and US gold futures for December falling 0.4% to $4,057.30 per ounce. This international movement was weighed down by higher oil prices and ongoing concerns regarding supply disruptions in the Middle East. Investors globally remained cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement and subsequent press conference by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, seeking clues regarding future interest rate trajectories and inflation assessments.

Rate expectations play a crucial role in determining gold valuations because bullion does not yield interest, making lower borrowing costs more attractive to investors. Market participants were also awaiting the release of the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index to gauge inflationary pressures. Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee continued its positive momentum in the inter-bank market, appreciating by Rs0.03 against the US dollar to close at 276.77.

These market shifts matter because they reflect the delicate interplay between domestic economic indicators in Pakistan and global financial trends dictated by US monetary policy. As investors weigh geopolitical tensions and inflation risks, domestic bullion adjustments and currency fluctuations remain critical barometers for the country's economic health and investor sentiment.

stories.title: KSE-100 Surges 1,270 Points as Buying Pressure Overcomes Regional Pressures
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange experienced a strong rally on Wednesday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index closing 1,269.55 points, or 0.77%, higher at 165,736.76. Trading activity picked up significantly in the final hours of the session, driven by widespread investor interest despite lingering concerns over monetary tightening, geopolitical uncertainties involving Iran, Israel and the United States, and Brent crude hovering around $115 per barrel. The market opened at 164,830.55, touched an intra-day high of 166,100.34, and reached a low of 164,355.83.

Market sentiment was supported by the State Bank's recent 50-basis-point policy rate hike to 12%, which came in lower than anticipated and helped bolster commercial banks, fertilizer, automobile, and power stocks. Fauji Fertilizer led the market rally following a dividend announcement of Rs18.5 per share alongside earnings that met expectations. National Bank posted solid earnings that stimulated banking sector buying, while Hub Power contributed with a Rs5-per-share payout. Overall trading volumes rose to 578 million shares from the previous session's 402 million, with a total traded value of Rs26 billion across 496 companies.

According to market analysts, including Ahmed Sheraz of KASB KTrade and Nawaz Ali of JS Global, bullish momentum was reinforced by positive regional trends in Asian equities, which rose on artificial intelligence optimism and upcoming US corporate earnings. Analysts noted that easing geopolitical tensions or a drop in crude oil prices could further enhance market confidence. Topline Securities reported that downside movement during the session was restricted to 111 points. Meanwhile, the National Clearing Company noted that foreign investors were net sellers, offloading shares worth Rs624 million during the trading day.

stories.title: Federal Minister Directs PPRA to Implement Three-Year Defect Liability Period
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Establishment Division Senator Ahad Cheema has directed the Pakistan Public Procurement Regulatory Authority to enforce a defect liability period of at least three years for major construction projects, with plans to extend the rule to smaller projects in phases. The directive was issued during a high-level meeting in Islamabad aimed at discussing sector reforms, improving project delivery, and resolving challenges faced by the construction industry.

The meeting featured discussions regarding the proposed Construction Industry Development Authority Bill. Minister Cheema emphasized that the institutional structure requires further review, specifically examining whether to establish a single regulatory body or two separate entities for sector regulation and industry promotion. Officials including Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani and representatives from the Constructors Association of Pakistan were advised to hold additional consultations regarding the framework.

Discussions also addressed contractor retention money accumulated during defect liability periods, with a proposal to deposit these funds into interest-earning accounts where both principal and returns would be paid back to contractors after completion. Furthermore, the meeting reviewed applying the Dispute Avoidance or Adjudication Board mechanism to government projects. While the Constructors Association of Pakistan suggested a threshold for projects valued at Rs20 billion and above, Minister Cheema called for a lower threshold and additional stakeholder consultation.

The upcoming construction framework will also incorporate standards and rules from the International Federation of Consulting Engineers. Attendees at the planning session included Housing Secretary Captain (retd) Muhammad Mahmood, a Planning Commission member, the PPRA managing director, and other senior government and industry representatives.

stories.title: Michigan US Senate Race Tests Progressive Policies and Anti-Muslim Attacks
stories.summary:
The competitive US Senate race in Michigan between Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers is playing a critical role in determining control of the Senate, where Republicans currently hold a narrow 53-47 majority. Independent analysts view the contest as a toss-up, with a RealClearPolitics poll average showing El-Sayed leading by 2.5 percentage points in a state that Donald Trump carried by 1.4 points in 2024. The election is also serving as a major test of whether identity-based attacks against a Muslim candidate can succeed in a battleground state and how receptive Democratic voters are to progressive policies.

Throughout the closing weeks of the campaign, Rogers has sought to portray El-Sayed as an outsider and a national security threat, tying him to the Muslim Brotherhood and referencing a 2012 Egyptian-American group letter supporting former Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi. Trump and Rogers have leveled harsh rhetoric against El-Sayed, prompting a rare public rebuke from NAACP President Derrick Johnson, who condemned the tactics as racist and divisive. Meanwhile, El-Sayed has strongly disavowed any connection to the Muslim Brotherhood, and his campaign has dismissed the accusations as bad-faith attacks designed to depress Democratic turnout among Black and Jewish voters in the Detroit area.

Political scientists note that the attacks aim to paint El-Sayed as dangerous while questioning his mainstream appeal. At 41, El-Sayed has positioned himself as a leading progressive voice advocating for universal healthcare, lower working-class costs, and expanded social safety nets, while identifying as a capitalist. Rogers, 63, has campaigned as a pragmatic conservative focused on lowering costs, bolstering manufacturing, border security, and calling for an end to the conflict in Iran and trade disputes with Canada.

A victory for El-Sayed would make him the nation's first Muslim senator and provide a significant boost to the Democratic Party's left wing ahead of the 2028 presidential election. However, political analysts emphasize that the margin of victory and ticket-splitting will be crucial indicators for the party's future direction. Polling from Michigan State University's Institute for Public Policy and Social Research indicated that 38% of Michigan voters were less inclined to support a Muslim candidate.

stories.title: Hasan Raheem Submits Cultural Track 'Bewajah' for Grammy Award Consideration
stories.summary:
Pakistani singer Hasan Raheem has submitted his song 'Bewajah' for consideration at the 2027 Grammy Awards across two categories: Best Music Video and Best Global Music Performance. The submission was announced via an Instagram post on the Hasan Raheem Global page. While this submission does not guarantee a formal Grammy nomination, it places the track in contention for one of the music industry's most prestigious honors and highlights the artist's ongoing efforts to showcase the musical traditions of his native Gilgit-Baltistan.

Released in March 2026 and produced by Umair, 'Bewajah' combines contemporary Urdu lyrics with a bridge written in Shina, a regional language spoken in Gilgit-Baltistan. The musical arrangement blends emotional storytelling with sounds deeply rooted in Raheem's northern cultural background, creating a distinctive auditory experience that bridges regional heritage with modern mainstream appeal.

The accompanying music video plays a central role in the project, filmed against the dramatic mountainous terrain of Gilgit, Pakistan. It prominently features regional traditions, including traditional attire, local dances, and a freestyle polo match associated with the area's Shandur Polo Festival. Raheem stands out in the video wearing white attire and jewelry amidst dark-clad players and spectators, reinforcing the visual narrative of northern Pakistan's cultural identity.

Raheem previously gained prominence through popular tracks such as 'Aisay Kaisay' and 'Joona', alongside collaborative performances on Coke Studio Pakistan. By incorporating elements like freestyle polo and regional languages into his art, Raheem continues to bring the heritage of Gilgit-Baltistan to wider national and international audiences.

stories.title: Masood Alam Debuts Nine-Track Album Mohabbat-Naama in Karachi
stories.summary:
Musician, producer, composer, and vocalist Masood Alam is set to launch his debut music album, titled Mohabbat-Naama, during a pre-release event at the Pakistan American Cultural Centre in Karachi on October 16. After spending more than 15 years working behind the scenes in the commercial and advertising music sector, Alam is shifting his focus to present his own distinct artistic identity through a nine-track collection.

The upcoming showcase will feature screenings of music videos for all nine tracks, alongside a presentation detailing the creative journey and behind-the-scenes production of the album. Featured vocalists Neha Khan and Zoya Raza will participate alongside Alam in interviews and a question-and-answer session with members of the media, offering attendees a comprehensive look at the project prior to its official release.

Alam's extensive background in the commercial industry includes collaborations with prominent directors such as Ahsan Rahim, Mukhtar Zaidi, Nabeel Qureshi, Sibtain Shabbir, Raheel Faridi, and Jibran Baig. He has also worked closely with major advertising agencies, including Adcom, Ogilvy, Synergy, and Stimulus, and partnered with established music artists like Atif Aslam, Hadiqa Kiani, and Natasha Baig.

The newly unveiled album explores the complex emotional phases of romance and relationships. Its nine songs cover various thematic stages of love, ranging from initial attraction and deep longing to heartbreak, emotional upheaval, and reconciliation, as well as the potential for finding affection once again.

stories.title: Punjab Election Commission Issues Notices Over Code Violations in By-Polls
stories.summary:
Punjab Election Commissioner Sharifullah announced on Thursday that show-cause notices have been issued to Minister for Power Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Huzaifa Rehman for allegedly violating the election code of conduct under the Election Act 2017. Both federal officials were directed by provincial election authorities to submit their formal explanations by November 21.

The Dera Ghazi Khan district monitoring officer reported that Leghari participated in the election campaign for PML-N candidate Mahmood Leghari in the NA-185 constituency, thereby breaching official regulations that prohibit ministers and advisors from running election campaigns. Similarly, monitoring officials noted that SAPM Rehman intended to take part in local campaign activities for the PML-N candidate, prompting official scrutiny ahead of the upcoming polls.

In a separate incident, Faisalabad's district monitoring officer flagged State Minister for Interior Talal Chaudhry for repeated violations of the electoral code. Despite receiving multiple warnings and two prior notices, the state minister failed to comply with instructions, resulting in a Rs50,000 fine and a referral to the main election body for further disciplinary action.

Official campaigning for the upcoming by-elections across six National Assembly and seven provincial assembly constituencies in Punjab is scheduled to conclude at midnight on November 21, with the actual voting slated for November 23. The Election Commission of Pakistan has cautioned that candidates and officials engaging in political activities past the deadline will face strict legal consequences, including potential fines of up to Rs100,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both.

stories.title: Pakistani Minister Says Federal Constitutional Court Alone Hears Constitutional Cases
stories.summary:
State Minister for Law Aqeel Malik stated on Thursday that the 27th Amendment grants the Federal Constitutional Court exclusive authority to hear constitutional cases, rather than the Supreme Court. Speaking on Geo News, Malik questioned why four Islamabad High Court judges attempted to file a petition in the Supreme Court, noting that the apex court is not the correct venue for such requests.

Malik rejected allegations of compromising judicial independence, explaining that the authority to transfer judges has been shifted from the president to the Judicial Commission. He also addressed judicial departures, remarking that resigning is a personal choice for judges and that misleading narratives are being circulated about these exits.

Sources indicated that Islamabad High Court Justices Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, Babar Sattar, Saman Rafat Imtiaz, and Sardar Ejaz Ishaq Khan prepared a draft petition to challenge the amendment in the Supreme Court. However, officials from both the Supreme Court and the Federal Constitutional Court confirmed that no such paperwork had been officially submitted to either institution.

The ruling coalition led by the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz enacted the 27th Amendment earlier this month, overhauling parts of the judicial framework and military leadership. The legislation established the Federal Constitutional Court with equal provincial representation and empowered it to exercise suo motu jurisdiction upon petitions.

The sweeping legal changes dissolved constitutional benches and transferred bench-forming powers to a three-member committee led by the chief justice via the Supreme Court Practice and Procedure Amendment Bill 2025. Following these developments, Supreme Court Justices Mansoor Ali Shah and Athar Minallah resigned, calling the amendment a grave assault on the constitution, while Lahore High Court Justice Shams Mehmood Mirza also quit in protest.

stories.title: Pakistan Air Force JF-17 Thunder Attracts Procurement Interest at Dubai Airshow
stories.summary:
Pakistan's JF-17 Thunder aircraft drew notable interest at the Dubai Airshow 2025, resulting in a procurement memorandum of understanding with a friendly nation. The Inter-Services Public Relations described the agreement as a significant milestone in expanding the nation's defence and industrial partnerships while reflecting growing global trust in its aviation sector.

Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, Chief of the Air Staff, engaged in several discussions with international counterparts on the sidelines of the event. He met with United Arab Emirates Undersecretary of Defence Lieutenant General Pilot Ibrahim Nasser Al-Alawi and UAE Air Force and Air Defence Commander Major General Rashid Mohammed Al-Shamsi to discuss advanced training, aerospace technologies, and operational coordination.

During the meetings, UAE military leadership commended the modernization efforts and growing indigenous capabilities of the Pakistan Air Force. Pakistan's exhibition contingent at the airshow featured the advanced JF-17 Thunder Block-III alongside the Super Mushshak trainer aircraft.

The operational capabilities of the JF-17 Thunder Block-III were highlighted following its performance during Marka-e-Haq, Pakistan's military response to Indian aggression in May. During that four-day conflict, Pakistan utilized the jets and hypersonic missiles to destroy an Indian S-400 air defence system in Adampur, besides downing multiple fighter jets and striking over twenty military sites in retaliation for earlier missile strikes.

stories.title: US Lawmakers Applaud Punjab's Brick-Kiln Modernisation Reforms
stories.summary:
Members of the Congressional Pakistan Caucus have formally praised the Punjab government's ongoing initiative to modernise its brick-kiln sector. In a letter directed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, US Congressmen Thomas Suozzi and Jack Bergman commended the provincial leadership's visionary efforts. They highlighted that these reforms could effectively function as a pilot project for eliminating bonded labour and drawing ethical foreign investments.

The lawmakers referenced the 2022 Trafficking in Persons Report published by the US State Department, pointing out that over 4.5 million individuals in Pakistan remain trapped within the peshgi system, a deeply rooted bonded labour practice. According to recent briefings received by the caucus, the provincial administration has demonstrated a firm commitment to carrying out this transformative initiative.

The communication stressed that mechanising and modernising the brick-kiln industry would assist Pakistan in fulfilling international commitments. Furthermore, it would render Punjab an increasingly appealing destination for foreign direct investment, specifically targeting American enterprises seeking ethical and sustainable partnerships.

The Congressional Pakistan Caucus underlined that these administrative and industrial reforms will boost bilateral economic relations and further solidify the broader Pakistan-US partnership. Reaffirming their backing, the lawmakers noted that Punjab is ideally positioned to act as a pilot province and encouraged local leadership to seek assistance whenever necessary.

stories.title: Security Forces Eliminate 30 Terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Operations
stories.summary:
Pakistan security forces neutralised 30 terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy Fitna al-Khawarij during a series of intelligence-based operations conducted across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, encounters took place in the Mohmand, Lakki Marwat, Tank, and Kurram districts over multiple days in November.

The military's media wing reported that an initial operation in Mohmand district on November 18-19 resulted in four deaths, while subsequent exchanges in Lakki Marwat and Tank accounted for three more militants. In Kurram district, targeted operations launched on November 19 eliminated a total of 23 terrorists across two separate engagements as troops capitalized on local intelligence.

These counter-terrorism actions form part of the broader Azm-e-Istehkam operation aimed at eradicating militancy amid a nationwide surge in violence since 2021. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded over 600 terror incidents during the first eight months of 2025, resulting in the deaths of 79 police personnel and 138 civilians. The security situation has also impacted other regions, highlighted by a recent suicide bombing in Islamabad that claimed 12 lives.

Pakistan continues to urge Afghanistan and the international community to address militant safe havens across the border, specifically targeting the outlawed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan. Meanwhile, a report presented to the UN Security Council by Denmark's Deputy Permanent Representative Sandra Jensen Landi confirmed that the TTP continues to orchestrate high-profile attacks from Afghan soil with logistical support from de facto authorities.

stories.title: MQM-P Renews Demand for New Province in Sindh Province
stories.summary:
The Muttahida Qaumi Movement–Pakistan has reiterated its long-standing demand for the creation of a new administrative province in Sindh. During a press conference in Karachi, MQM-P convener Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui outlined plans for an upcoming public mobilisation campaign and legal actions to secure constitutional rights for urban residents, warning that the party would take its struggle to the streets if parliament and the courts failed to deliver justice.

Siddiqui stated that the demand aligns with Article 239 of the Constitution, which permits the formation of new provinces and districts. He argued that administrative units must expand alongside population growth and criticized the existing governance structure, claiming that Karachi has endured a 17-year occupation under a feudal democracy that denies urban centers their fair share of authority and resources.

The MQM-P leader questioned why opponents of a new province in Sindh do not hold a similar stance regarding the division of Punjab. He also stressed the importance of fully implementing the 18th Amendment and Article 140-A to ensure empowered local governments, criticizing the marginalization of municipal issues in Karachi and Hyderabad.

Sindh Governor Kamran Tessori echoed these sentiments during the briefing, asserting that genuine relief for citizens will only arrive when the MQM-P governs the entire province. Tessori vowed to support Siddiqui's demands and highlighted ongoing public grievances regarding deteriorating infrastructure and neglected local services.

stories.title: US Report Confirms Pakistan Military Superiority Over India, Says PM
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that a recent report submitted to the US Congress formally validates Pakistan's military strength and its successful aerial engagements against India during a conflict earlier this year. Speaking at a foundation-laying ceremony for a Danish School in Bagh, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, the prime minister declared that the Pakistan Air Force and army forced India to yield within four days.

The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission report acknowledged Pakistan's military success in the May conflict, noting the deployment of advanced Chinese weaponry—including J-10C fighter jets, HQ-9 air-defence systems, and PL-15 missiles—to secure a tactical edge. The report highlighted that the clashes, which followed Indian strikes in response to a deadly attack in Pahalgam, involved deep territorial penetrations by both nuclear-armed nations before a US-brokered ceasefire on May 10.

Prime Minister Shehbaz also linked the battlefield performance to international recognition, pointing to repeated praise from former US President Donald Trump. He claimed that the Pakistan Air Force downed multiple Indian aircraft, including Rafales, and successfully destroyed India's S-400 air defence system using hypersonic missiles during Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos.

Shifting focus to education during the event, the prime minister emphasized the expansion of the Danish Schools network, which provides free merit-based education and lodging. He announced that the Bagh campus will officially open on March 23, 2026, and confirmed plans to establish another campus in Forward Kahuta.

stories.title: UNSC Panel Warns TTP Poses Major Security Threat to Pakistan
stories.summary:
A UN Security Council panel has warned that the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan continues to pose a severe and expanding regional danger. Speaking to the 15-member Council, Denmark's Deputy Permanent Representative Sandra Jensen Landi stated that the group comprises about 6,000 fighters and benefits from substantial logistical and practical backing from the Afghan de facto authorities, having launched several major attacks inside Pakistan.

During the briefing, Pakistan's Deputy Permanent Representative Usman Jadoon highlighted the nation's heavy toll in combating terrorism, noting over 80,000 casualties and massive economic losses. Jadoon criticized regional actors and accused Afghan hosts of sheltering militant groups such as ISIL-K, the TTP, and the Balochistan Liberation Army.
