He also urged that UN sanctions mechanisms remain transparent and fair while addressing all forms of extremism.

Tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have recently spiked following cross-border clashes. Following unprovoked aggression on October 12, the Pakistan Armed Forces reported killing over 200 militants and Afghan Taliban forces in self-defense, while suffering 23 soldier casualties. Subsequent peace talks in Doha and Istanbul failed to produce a lasting agreement due to a lack of cooperation from Kabul.

Meanwhile, China voiced support for designating the Balochistan Liberation Army and its Majeed Brigade under UN terror lists to reinforce a global zero-tolerance stance. The Security Council continues to monitor evolving terrorist threats globally as member states debate stricter counter-terrorism protocols and enforcement tools.

stories.title: KP Chief Minister Clarifies Remarks Following ECP Army Deployment Request
stories.summary:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has clarified his recent remarks regarding an upcoming by-election after the Election Commission of Pakistan requested the deployment of the army and civil armed forces. The electoral body acted in response to what it labeled as threatening and provocative statements made by the chief minister directed at public officials and police.

Speaking to journalists in Rawalpindi, Afridi maintained that his speech during a political gathering in Chamba was misinterpreted and taken completely out of context. He asserted that he was merely advocating against electoral rigging and stated that authorities had repeatedly blocked his requests to visit imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan.

The ECP formally wrote to the Ministries of Defense and Interior, expressing serious concern that the chief minister's Haripur speech created direct threats to election workers, police officers, and voters. The electoral body argued that Afridi's language violated election laws and codes of conduct that prohibit provincial chief executives from joining active election campaigns or intimidating administrative staff.

In response to the escalating situation, the ECP summoned relevant officials, including the KP inspector general and the provincial election commissioner, for a formal assessment meeting. Furthermore, the commission warned that strict legal actions will be enforced against any individual attempting to interfere with the peaceful administration of the vote.

stories.title: Dubai International Airport Welcomes 3.2 Million Pakistani Passengers in 2025
stories.summary:
Dubai International Airport handled 3.2 million passengers traveling from Pakistan during the first nine months of 2025, solidifying the country as the airport's fourth-largest market. Dubai Airports noted that millions of travelers continuously depend on the hub for tourism, business trips, family visits, job opportunities, and onward connections throughout Europe, the Middle East, and North America.

Overall, the airport registered its highest quarterly traffic in its 65-year history by welcoming 24.2 million passengers between July and September, marking a 1.9 percent year-on-year increase. Total passenger volume from January through September climbed to 70.1 million, reflecting a 2.1 percent growth compared to the previous year, while 12-month rolling traffic reached a record 93.8 million.

India remained the top market for the airport with 8.8 million travelers, followed by Saudi Arabia with 5.5 million and the United Kingdom with 4.6 million. Pakistan secured the fourth position ahead of the United States, maintaining its status as a vital partner for tourism and labor mobility within the United Arab Emirates.

Operational efficiency remained high, with nearly all visitors passing through security and passport controls rapidly. Specifically, 99.6 percent of departing passengers cleared checks in under ten minutes, while 99.8 percent of arrivals finished immigration in less than 15 minutes. Facility upgrades across Terminals 1 and 3 are also underway to accommodate expanding South Asian travel demand.

stories.title: Security Forces Eliminate 23 Terrorists in Separate Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Operations
stories.summary:
Pakistani security forces neutralised 23 Indian proxy Fitna al-Khawarij militants during separate engagements in the Kurram district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on November 19. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, the first targeted operation relied on intelligence regarding militant presence and resulted in 12 terrorists being killed following an intense exchange of fire.

Capitalizing on further intelligence about another group hiding in the same vicinity, troops conducted a second intelligence-based operation that successfully eliminated 11 additional militants. Sanitisation procedures were subsequently launched to clear the area of any remaining threats, with the military reaffirming its commitment to eradicating foreign-sponsored terrorism under the Azm-e-Istehkam counterterrorism campaign.

These actions form part of a broader nationwide counterterrorism effort that has neutralized dozens of fighters in recent days. Previous operations between November 16 and 18 led to the deaths of four militants in Bajaur, Spinwam, Zakir Khel, and Dera Ismail Khan, following another 23 casualties from intelligence-based operations in Bajaur and Bannu.

The security sweeps follow a rise in militant violence across Pakistan, notably a November 11 suicide bombing at the Islamabad Judicial Complex that killed 12 people and wounded 36 others. Border provinces Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan continue to face the heaviest toll, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recording over 600 terror incidents and numerous casualties among police and civilians during the first eight months of 2025, while Islamabad urges the Afghan Taliban to uphold the 2020 Doha agreement.

stories.title: Pakistan Petroleum Limited Plans Artificial Island to Support Offshore Oil Drilling
stories.summary:
State-owned Pakistan Petroleum Limited has announced plans to build an artificial island off the coast of Sindh near Sujawal to accelerate oil exploration activities. The initiative follows intensified drilling plans prompted by US President Donald Trump expressing interest in Pakistan's oil reserves and a recent study pointing to significant undiscovered hydrocarbons in offshore basins.

According to Bloomberg, Arshad Palekar, general manager of exploration and core business development at Pakistan Petroleum Limited, stated that the launchpad will stand six feet above the water to protect round-the-clock operations from high tides. Speaking at an Islamabad energy conference, Palekar noted that the project is a first for Pakistan and draws inspiration from Abu Dhabi's successful implementation of artificial islands for drilling.

Construction of the artificial island is scheduled for completion in February, with exploration drilling expected to begin immediately afterward. The company intends to drill approximately 25 wells from the facility, according to the exploration official.

The announcement comes weeks after the Ministry of Energy awarded 23 offshore exploration blocks on October 31 to four consortia of local and international companies. This marked Pakistan's first competitive bidding round in roughly two decades, covering roughly 53,500 square kilometers across 40 offered blocks. The push aligns with statements made in July by US President Trump, who announced on Truth Social that his administration finalized a partnership deal with Pakistan to develop the country's massive oil reserves.
